229de5ddde29180ed38d5894fcceff28ef537e5d.caption: Don't example: a red error toast with error icon, the text "Some required fields are left empty" and a close button, used for important information. This is wrong because toasts disappear, lie above the content and cannot be reached by keyboard.

4cc98f46c0490e55f574857ad24ded4144a9bd87.caption: Green success toast with check icon, the text "All files updated" and a close button. A purple clock badge labelled "10 sec" below it indicates the time the toast stays visible.

4e944c7a482f13d2a8ecabd255ca8c53ba23653b.caption: Do example: a grey info toast with info icon, the text "A new update is available" and a close button. This is right because the message is very short, ideally below 5 words.

79912186fe2c935d301c3dc2c06b4853f5e8f2a5.caption: Do example: a filled "Copy number" button with a copy icon on the right, in hover / pressed state with a mouse cursor on it, followed by an arrow pointing to an info toast reading "Number copied to clipboard" with a close button. 87575198ef625539255aa6ad835bfbfabb2d9427.caption: Left, a dashed purple frame with three stacked toasts with the text "All files lorem ipsum": success (green, check icon), warning (yellow, warning icon) and info (grey, info icon), each with a close button on the right. 9ce10fa65945f90bc54557e6702432bba6673c65.caption: Don't example: a toast with a round profile photo of a person on the left, the text "Susie sent you a personal message" and a ghost close button on the right. Images such as photos or avatars must not be used in toast notifications.

Toasts must not be stacked; they should be shown one after another in a queue.
